aws_opendata_registry.Name: Satellite - Surface Waves - CFOSAT SWIM off-nadir wave spectra - Delayed mode
aws_opendata_registry.Description:
This dataset contains global daily wave observations from the Surface Wave Investigation and Monitoring (SWIM) instrument onboard the China-France Oceanography Satellite (CFOSAT), a joint mission of the French (CNES) and Chinese (CNSA) space agencies launched in October 2018. SWIM is a Ku-band real-aperture wave scatterometer with six rotating beams at incidence angles from 0° to 10°. Because its footprint rotates around the nadir, SWIM views the ocean surface from all azimuths and retrieves directional ocean wave spectra, in addition to integrated wave parameters.

The SWIM Level-2 data (source: CNES) have been aggregated into 1° by 1° geographical bins and homogenised into a consistent, easily usable format. Each record is one satellite pass over a bin and includes:
- the 2D wave slope spectrum from the 10° beam (MSS), and a mean wave slope spectrum combining all incidence beams (MSS_COMBINED), on 32 wavenumbers (wavelengths of about 23–500 m) and 12 directions (0–180°, with the inherent 180° directional ambiguity)
- SWIM Level-2 standard wave parameters from the 10° beam: significant wave height (SWH), dominant wavelength (Lp) and dominant direction (Dp)
- an improved mean wave period (MWP) estimate based on Jiang et al. (2022)
- SWH, Lp and MWP calibrated against in-situ NDBC wave buoy observations (*_CALIBRATED_NDBC)
- collocated WAVEWATCH III hindcast model outputs (SWH, Lp, MWP, Dp) for comparison
- ancillary information: nadir rain flag percentage, land and sea-ice coverage, distance to coast and bathymetry (GEBCO 2019)

All variables carry IMOS standard quality control flags. The record covers April 2019 to October 2024.

This is a trial dataset, and its calibration and validation is an area of current active research.

The dataset is produced by CSIRO and distributed by the Australian Ocean Data Network (AODN) as part of the Integrated Marine Observing System (IMOS).
